title: Adi / shared material palettes
principle: Palettes reference canonical names; no texture or material copies.
status: Concept appearance library, not construction specifications or measured environmental performance.

palettes.name: Adi / house palette
palettes.intent: A reusable family of warm mineral surfaces, named colours, timber and restrained metal. Projects choose a subset and declare their own roles; they do not inherit a uniform style.

roles.guidance: Choose the material from construction and exposure, then use its canonical appearance.
Reserve finer stone for thresholds and civic edges; coordinate joints and slip resistance at specification stage.
Named appearance colours. These entries do not certify lime content, coating chemistry or heritage approval.
Use on shutters, doors or small accents, with variation by building address.
Walnut for sheltered joinery; Teak is an existing visual surrogate for warm exterior timber, not a species or durability specification.
Dark rails, muted roofs and limited brass accents. BIMCraft Glass Grey is an opaque concept appearance.

palettes.name: Ansonborough / western quarter
palettes.intent: Brick houses, side piazzas and garden thresholds within denser contemporary blocks.

roles.guidance: Brick is the primary family; light painted addresses break up the frontage.
Light cornices and sheltered timber details frame the planted side courts.
Dark details read against warm walls.
A quiet roof line and distinct pedestrian thresholds.

palettes.name: French Quarter / southern streets
palettes.intent: Layered commercial streets and intimate passages, interpreted through differentiated frontages and sheltered edges.

roles.guidance: Alternate colours by coherent frontage, not random panels; keep some masonry visible.
Deep galleries, fine dark rails and selected shutters establish a residential grain.
Muted roof surfaces and durable street thresholds.

palettes.name: Northern courts / civic accents
palettes.intent: Larger masonry courts with selected vertical accents; this is a project interpretation, not a claim that the northern neighbourhood is historically Gothic.

roles.guidance: Group masonry by building, with stone at public entrances and selected landmarks.
Steep roof silhouettes and dark openings support the larger massing.
A restrained light edge distinguishes the upper storeys.

palettes.name: Harbour / contemporary market
palettes.intent: A lighter, contemporary family for the fixed terrace, generous market halls and timber pier.

roles.guidance: A warm timber appearance follows the deck strips. Final exterior species, treatment and wet slip resistance remain to be selected.
Quiet mineral bodies, muted metal roofs, glazed openings and timber fins.
Express the structural base separately from the timber deck.
Stone at the fixed public ground and dark rails along water-facing edges.
